steps.say: Every coding agent runs this loop. The model asks for a tool, the harness runs it, the result goes back in.
Everything outside the model is the harness. So what happens if you keep the model and swap the harness?

scenes.headline: Same model, four harnesses, one bill each
scenes.sub: Qwen3.8-27B on an RTX 3090, metered request by request
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nib. I ran four open source coding harnesses against one local model and counted every token.

steps.say: Thirteen small repositories, each with a test suite that fails until the bug is fixed.
Each harness gets the same prompt, twice per task, inside a sandbox.
A proxy in the middle forces the same sampling and logs every request.
steps.term: Proxy: counts tokens without trusting the harness

steps.say: llama.cpp serves it, and reuses any prompt prefix it has already seen.
And one model behind all of it, quantised to fit a single twenty-four gigabyte card.

states.say: And almost all of them pass. pi and OpenCode solve every task. The other two miss one each.

steps.say: The difference starts before any history. OpenCode's first request carries ten tools and a long system prompt. pi's carries four.
steps.term: Prefix: what is re-sent on every request

steps.say: That prefix rides along on every request, so a whole run grows to match.
OpenCode sends about four times pi's prompt for the same fixes.

scenes.title: Input-token equivalents, whole run
scenes.note: cache reads priced at a tenth of the input rate
scenes.say: Locally the cache hides most of it. On a metered API it does not. Price cache reads at a tenth, and OpenCode costs three times what pi does.

items.say: Aider has no tools. The model reads a map of the repository and names the files it wants.
In the second request it writes search and replace blocks, and Aider applies them.
Fewest tokens of all four. But the file contents arrive late, so only half its prompt is reused from cache.

scenes.label: prompt tokens in one mini-swe-agent run that never stopped
scenes.say: The most expensive run was a failure. mini-swe-agent went round sixty times on one task, two thirds of everything it sent. Only the step limit stopped it.

steps.caption: same model, different harness
steps.say: On harder benchmarks the harness moves the score too. Here, on one model, a searched harness beats Claude Code's own.

scenes.text: On easy work the harness sets the bill, not the score. Check the prefix and the stopping rule.
scenes.mark: the prefix and the stopping rule
scenes.say: On work a strong model can do, the harness sets the bill, not the score. Look at what it sends every time, and at what stops it.
Same model, same tasks, a four times spread in tokens. Thanks for watching!
